sections.h2: What makes Pickens County, Georgia, different for a home seller?
sections.html:
Pickens County sits in the north Georgia mountains with Jasper as its seat, and it skews older and pricier than its neighbors in this comparison. Pickens County grew to an estimated 37,167 residents by mid-2025, and seniors are 26.8 percent of residents. The county covers 232.06 square miles of land at 143.1 people per square mile.

Pickens has the priciest typical home of the four counties compared, at $332,700, and 81.2 percent of its housing is lived in by the owner. Median gross rent was $1,136. Builders took out 277 permits in 2025. Health care and social assistance receipts reached $222,994 thousand in 2022, second only to Paulding among the four counties. Retail sales per capita came to $20,835.

A senior-heavy owner base matters for tax questions, because Pickens County has local exemptions that older owners may already hold. A buyer who loses those exemptions at closing may see a different bill than the seller paid, and sellers who understand that can explain it before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: Who bills and who values property in Pickens County?
sections.html:
The Pickens County Tax Commissioner bills, collects and distributes, and also processes motor vehicle registration. The Board of Tax Assessors appraises property, approves exemptions and reviews appeals. Grand jurors appoint the Board of Equalization that hears the administrative appeal.

Pickens County tax contacts, per the commissioner's website
ItemDetail
Tax Commissioner address1266 E. Church Street, Jasper, GA 30143
Tax Commissioner phone(706) 253-8882

Commissioner office hoursMonday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The commissioner's news box also mentions a drop box that is open around the clock in front of the Administration Building. Using a card costs a 2.60 percent convenience fee at the counter, on the web or by phone. An e-check adds a flat $3.00. Partial payments are welcome, though interest keeps running on whatever stays unpaid. The same site lets owners ask online for a mailing address change, and it keeps forms, an excess funds page and a tax sale page for bidder registration.

sections.h2: What are the Pickens County tax deadlines and late costs?
sections.html:
November 15 is the commissioner's date for real estate and business personal property. Manufactured homes get a January bill and an April 1 deadline. A US Postal Service postmark counts as timely, but a metered postmark does not.

The FAQ page describes the consequences of paying late:

  • Interest of 0.8750 percent was added for 2025 bills, and from January 2026 the rate is prime plus 3 percent divided across 12 months.
  • The commissioner's news box says a 5 percent penalty comes at day 120, recurs every 120 days and stops at 20 percent.
  • Taxes more than 90 days late can lead to a recorded FIFA lien at the courthouse.
  • The office can levy on the property but calls that a last resort.

Mail goes to the homeowner only, never the lender, so an owner with an escrow account has to pass the bill along. If you sell near the due date, ask whether the lender already paid.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Pickens County assessment?
sections.html:
Day 45 after the notice date is the last day. The Board of Tax Assessors looks again at its value first and responds with a decision. Where the board holds firm, the Board of Equalization takes the appeal up at a hearing. Superior Court is the final stop.

Some details from the commissioner's general information page:

  • You can appeal on taxability, value, uniformity compared with similar property, or the denial of an exemption.
  • You can request arbitration at the time of filing instead of going to the Board of Equalization.
  • Filing a return happens at the assessors' office in the first three months. Filing one that declares your own value can preserve appeal rights if the board later changes the number.
  • Taxable value begins at 40 percent of market value. County commissioners and the school board each pick a millage rate.

Ask the assessors for the exact mailing date on your notice, since the 45 days count from that date and not from the day it reaches you.

sections.h2: What exemptions can a Pickens County homeowner use?
sections.html:
The standard homestead subtracts $2,000 from assessed value before the county, school and State operating rates are applied. The Board of Tax Assessors accepts applications, and the books close April 1. Anything received later counts toward the following year. New owners should carry in a copy of their warranty deed.

The commissioner's page lists several age and service exemptions:

  • One Pickens-only exemption erases the school levy for owners aged 62 or older with a gross household income of $25,000 or under.
  • A standard elderly school exemption of up to $10,000 for owners 62 or older whose net income does not exceed $10,000.
  • A general elderly exemption of up to $4,000 for owners 65 or older under the same income limit.
  • A disabled veteran exemption of up to $50,000 of assessed value.
  • A deferral that postpones the bill without erasing it, open to owners 62 or older with household income at or below $15,000.

A floating exemption is open to owners 62 or older whose income is $30,000 or lower. It stands in for other state and county exemptions, and the commissioner warns that the first bill may rise. Ask the assessors before applying for it.

sections.h2: How should I handle property tax when selling a Pickens County house?
sections.html:
Dial (706) 253-8882 to learn what the parcel owes, and ask if earlier years, interest or a lien are involved. The commissioner's site has a tax sale page with procedures and a bidder registration form, which tells you how the office handles properties that stay delinquent.

The sale contract, applied by the closing attorney, sets the split of the year's tax. If the seller held an elderly or local school exemption, the buyer starts without it and must apply for a homestead on the new home. Deed copies are kept by the Clerk of Superior Court.

Mobile homes on the lot are billed in January with an April 1 due date and need a current decal, which is issued when the tax is paid. If a mobile home sits on the lot, ask the commissioner whether it carries a separate bill before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What will a buyer moving into a Pickens County home need from the tax office?
sections.html:
A buyer who relocates from another state will deal with the same Jasper office that bills the house. The commissioner also registers vehicles, and its new-resident page names what a person needs to tag a car in Pickens County. Mention this to buyers early, because it saves a second trip.

  • For a car with no loan: the out-of-state title, the registration from the previous state, proof of Georgia insurance, a Georgia driver's license showing a Pickens County address, and the current mileage.
  • For a car with a loan: the loan agreement with the lender's full name and address, the T-17 affidavit of the lienholder, and the same insurance, license and mileage items.

The license requirement means a buyer should update the address on the license after closing. The commissioner's site posts a link for searching property and mobile home taxes online, so a buyer can check the parcel's bill history before signing.

faqs.q: What is the Pickens County property tax due date?
faqs.a: The commissioner's site gives November 15 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1.

faqs.q: How can I pay a Pickens County tax bill?
faqs.a: Walk-in payments take check, cash or card. Online payment takes cards and e-checks. A drop box outside the Administration Building stays open day and night. Cards add a 2.60 percent fee and e-checks add $3.00.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal in Pickens County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, starting on the date of the assessment notice. Step one is the Board of Tax Assessors. Step two is the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator.

faqs.q: Does a Pickens County homeowner need to reapply for homestead after buying?
faqs.a: Yes. A new owner or new residence must apply again, and the assessors need it by April 1 for it to count that year.

faqs.q: Does late Pickens County property tax hurt my credit?
faqs.a: It can. Lien filings at the courthouse are public, and the commissioner notes that credit bureaus may pick them up.
